title: Ready for Winter! Animal Coats and Dens for Kids
description:
How do animals get ready for winter? Pick your answer with Milo the bluebird, then find out: an arctic fox grows a thick white coat and furry paws for the snow, a polar bear's white-looking fur covers black skin and a thick layer of fat, and a brown bear digs a den and can stay inside for up to seven months.
An interactive animal lesson for kids ages 2-6, with questions to answer, counting, actions to copy, quick checks and a quiz at the end.
facts: Arctic fox: the white phase has a thick, white coat during the colder, winter months; in summer the coat ranges from gray to brown on the back; paws are sheathed in dense fur during the winter; dense, bushy coat; long, fluffy tail (SeaWorld Parks & Entertainment animal info 'Arctic Fox', seaworld.org/animals/facts/mammals/arctic-fox, read Nov 17 2026).

Polar bear: hair is see-through with no pigment, so it looks white; black nose, skin and claws; covered with fur except for the nose; subcutaneous fat 5-10 cm thick in adults; ears relatively small; tail 7-12 cm; even foot pads may be furred during winter (SDZWA Library fact sheet 'Polar Bear', Physical Characteristics, ielc.libguides.com/sdzg/factsheets/polarbear/characteristics, read Nov 17 2026). Thick fat layer and fur to stay warm in extreme Arctic temperatures (fact sheet summary page, read Nov 17 2026).

Brown bear: in cold climates undergo winter dormancy; farthest north habitats up to 7 months; dens in dug earth have a tunnel about 4 feet long leading to a chamber 5 feet in diameter; dens are excavated as early as September or immediately before use in November; often stand while stopped; relies mainly on a sense of smell (SDZWA Library fact sheet 'Brown Bear', Behavior & Ecology, ielc.libguides.com/sdzg/factsheets/brownbear/behavior, read Nov 17 2026).

segments.name: hello
lines: Hello, friends! I am Milo the bluebird.
Today we are learning about how animals get ready for winter!
Coats, fat and cozy dens. Who does what?
Three animal friends will show us. Count them with me. One, two, three!
Put on your warm coat. Let's go!

segments.name: arctic_fox

lines.t: Who grows a thick, white coat for the snowy winter?
Is it the arctic fox? Or is it the pig?

lines: It is the arctic fox!
Here is the fun fact. In winter, this arctic fox has a thick, white coat.
White, like the snow all around it. Fluffy and warm! Can you spot it in the snow?

lines.t: What color is its coat in summer, when the snow is gone? Hmm.

lines: In summer, its coat turns gray and brown on its back!
Look at that fluffy, white fox!
close:arctic_fox
In winter, its paws are covered in thick fur too. Furry paws, like warm boots!
Furry paws, on the cold, cold snow. Tip, tap, tip, tap.
And it has a long, fluffy tail. So bushy, and so soft!
White coat, furry paws, and a fluffy tail. This fox is ready for winter!
Say it with me. An arctic fox has a white winter coat!
close:host
Can you tiptoe like a fox on the snow? Tip, tap, tip, tap!
Now wag a big, fluffy tail. Swish, swish!

lines.t: Quick check! What color is the arctic fox's winter coat? White? Or purple?

lines: White! Like the snow. Great job!

short.title: Why Is This Arctic Fox White? Arctic Fox Facts

segments.name: polar_bear

lines.t: Who has fur that looks white, with black skin underneath?
Is it the polar bear? Or is it the cow?

lines: It is the polar bear!
Here is the fun fact. Under its fur, a polar bear's skin is black!
Its fur looks white, but each hair is see-through, like glass. Wow! Isn't that amazing?

lines.t: What else keeps a polar bear warm, under its skin? Hmm.

lines: A thick layer of fat! Up to four inches thick. Warm and cozy!
Look at that big, fluffy bear!
close:polar_bear
Thick fur and thick fat keep it warm, in the freezing cold Arctic.
Fur everywhere, except its nose. Its nose is black, too! Black nose, black skin!
A polar bear has small ears, and a short little tail.
Small ears, a short tail, and a big, fluffy body! What a bear!
Say it with me. A polar bear has black skin!
close:host
Can you hug yourself, warm and cozy like a polar bear? Squeeze!
Now touch your nose. Boop! A polar bear's nose is black.

lines.t: Quick check! Is a polar bear's skin black? Yes, or no?

lines: Yes! Black skin, under white-looking fur. You remembered!

short.title: What Color Is a Polar Bear's Skin? Polar Bear Facts

segments.name: bear

lines.t: Who sleeps in a cozy den, all winter long?
Is it the brown bear? Or is it the pig?

lines: It is the brown bear!
Here is the fun fact. In cold places, a brown bear spends the winter in a den.
A den is a cozy room, under the ground. Snug and safe!

lines.t: How long can a brown bear stay in its den? Hmm.

lines: In the coldest places, up to seven months! That is most of the year.
Look at that sleepy brown bear!
close:bear
A brown bear digs its own den. A tunnel, then a round room at the end.
Some bears start digging their den in September! Dig, dig, dig!
A brown bear uses its nose to learn about the world around it. Sniff, sniff!
And a brown bear often stands up tall, on its back legs, to look around.
Say it with me. A brown bear sleeps in a den!
close:host
Can you dig like a bear? Dig, dig, dig, with both paws!
Now curl up in your den, and take a little nap. Shh.

lines.t: Quick check! Where does a brown bear spend the winter? In a den? Or up a tree?

lines: In a den! Cozy and snug. Super thinking!

short.title: Where Does a Brown Bear Sleep in Winter?

segments.name: quiz
lines: Wow! We met three friends who are ready for winter. Now it is quiz time!
Get ready. Think hard!
quiz: Who grows a white coat for the snow?
Who has black skin under its fur?
Who sleeps in a den all winter?

segments.name: goodbye
lines: You learned so many new things today.
A white coat like a fox. Thick fat like a polar bear. And a cozy den like a brown bear!
What do you wear when it is cold outside?
Thank you for learning with me. Bye-bye, friends! See you next time!
